LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up slightly, and while its profit margins are running below where they've historically been, defense spending remains a steady tailwind, so the business itself is intact.

ASML.sentence: ASML has pulled back about 25% from its high, which is a real dip, but nothing has changed about the fact that they're the only company in the world making a certain essential chipmaking machine.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly doing its job — when the broader market wobbled, this industrial gas supplier actually held up better, which is exactly the steady, dependable role it plays.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is down a touch but holding up better than its peers — the cloud-and-AI story keeps grinding along without any real drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is quiet; the lab-equipment business has already recovered a good chunk of its earlier slump, so there's less room for a big jump from here.

CVX.sentence: Chevron edged up with oil prices that are swollen by Middle East disruptions — that makes its profits look unusually big right now, but that's the oil price doing the work, not the company suddenly getting better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen sharply, down nearly half from its high, even though big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-assistant tools — so this looks more like a price reset than a business problem.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a few percent today even as copper itself rose, an odd disconnect for a company that mines copper and trades commodities — worth watching whether the stock catches back up.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose a bit, and the part that actually matters is healthy — the price they get per ton of crushed stone keeps creeping up and they're shipping a little more rock, which is the whole engine of this business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA ticked up, but a weakening Mexican peso quietly eats into what their Latin American sales are worth once converted into dollars, which is the main thing to watch here.

UBER.sentence: Uber climbed, and the key signal — how much people are booking in rides — was still growing strongly as of last quarter, with no sign that self-driving cars are pulling business away yet.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk fell over 6% and is now priced below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — a reminder that this container-shipping giant rises and falls with the health of global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard climbed, and interestingly it's trading unusually close to rival Visa rather than at its normal premium — people keep tapping cards more than ever, so the core toll-collecting business is humming along.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot maker dipped slightly, but it's cheaper relative to its own history than it's been in a while, even as hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines — and every operation sells more supplies.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell again after Google's parent and Amazon showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are the customers who pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
